title: Computational fluid dynamics investigation of a Stirling engine with one‐way oscillating flow cycle for efficient waste heat recovery
content:
Abstract

Facing the dual challenges of climate change and resource sustainability, efficient recovery of medium-low temperature industrial waste heat is crucial for achieving the “dual carbon” goals. Stirling engines (SEs) have emerged as a preferred solution due to their unique advantages. However, traditional cycles suffer irreversible heat loss from non-ideal isothermal heat transfer. The one-way oscillatory flow cycle (OOFC) offers an innovative fix by using adiabatic processes, yet existing low-order models fail to capture key 3D transient phenomena, causing large prediction deviations. Based on the GPU-3 benchmark, this study develops the first full 3D computational fluid dynamics OOFC engine model (OEM) with real geometries. Comparative analysis with the SE model, OEM achieves the first full-system 3D transient simulation of OOFC, which is not only capturing overlooked critical phenomena but also exhibits excellent performance: indicated power increases by 23.5% to 4993 W, thermal efficiency rises by 80% to 60%, and Relative Carnot efficiency jumps from 47% to 87%. Additionally, the OEM reduces the regenerator's peak temperature by 20%, facilitating structural simplification and cost reduction. This work provides a high precision numerical foundation for OOFC's engineering application, confirming its potential as an efficient, scalable waste heat recovery solution.
